parallel.requirements: The run recognized the clean-room task: infer Lua behavior by running the provided executable and bundled documentation, then produce an original executable without source-code lookup or wrapping.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent created a workflow to probe 16 behavior areas with area-specific child agents and critic follow-ups, while the parent retained implementation responsibility for the interpreter files.
parallel.implementation: The parent wrote partial C interpreter source including code, lexer, parser, object, and header files, but the artifact does not contain a complete interpreter or buildable submission.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The workflow produced notes and tests for some areas, with the patterns probe returning a detailed result, but most children remained in progress and the final artifact was partial with validation marked false.
parallel.verification: Verification was mostly behavioral probing and child regression scripts; no completed integrated build or evaluator-aligned acceptance run occurred before the official compile failure.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The workflow was killed and the agent timed out with return code 143, no final response, and a compile_failed official evaluation with all testcases not run.

serial.requirements: The serial run received the same prompt and recognized the need to reimplement Lua from observed binary behavior under the same clean-room restrictions.
serial.plan_and_ownership: The serial control had no delegation available; the single agent explored the workspace and proceeded locally toward a C bytecode VM and support structures.
serial.implementation: It created a smaller partial source tree, including mlua.h, table.c, and mem.c, and was about to continue into conversions and lexer work when it stopped.
serial.integration_and_delivery: No child results or integration boundary existed; the delivered artifact was only the partial local source tree and validation was marked false.
serial.verification: The serial attempt used local observation and source edits but did not deliver a completed build or whole-task verification before the official compile failure.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Although the process completed normally with budget remaining, the implementation was far short of a runnable Lua interpreter and the evaluator reported compile_failed with all tests not run.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the benchmark as a clean-room Lua behavioral reimplementation and encoded broad Lua subsystem requirements into workflow prompts.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial received the same prompt and README context and also worked toward a Lua interpreter reimplementation from observed behavior.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement disagreement drove the official result; both understood the broad target, but parallel externalized more behavioral coverage into child probes.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split investigation into many behavior-area child probes plus a critic phase while the parent remained the implementation actor.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had workflows and delegation disabled and therefore kept exploration and implementation in one local agent process.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel used broad concurrent research fan-out; serial used a linear single-owner implementation path.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child briefs specified exact behavioral-probe deliverables as notes and tests, not implementation component interfaces.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no cross-agent handoff or interface boundary; all knowledge and edits stayed in the single parent trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The key context difference was not a missing contract but the volume and lifecycle of delegated probe work versus serial local state.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel wrote a larger partial interpreter skeleton and patched parser/code files late in the run.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote only the initial memory/table/header portion of a C implementation and stopped before lexer/conversions were written.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel progressed further in source breadth but still not to a coherent complete implementation; serial had less source but did not time out.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel started many workflow children and received only the patterns result before the workflow state remained killed with most agents in progress.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle and its single agent completed normally.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel carried unresolved child results at closure; serial avoided that lifecycle but still stopped with unfinished implementation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel packed notes, tests, partial source, build directory, repository metadata, and executable into an artifact marked validation false.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial packed only a partial src tree plus repository metadata and executable, also with artifact validation false.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Neither delivered an integrated buildable final tree; parallel had more probe artifacts while serial had fewer implementation files and no workflow artifacts.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel had child-generated regression scripts for some areas, especially patterns, but no completed end-to-end build acceptance before evaluation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no comparable child test suite and likewise no completed build acceptance before evaluation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel gathered more behavioral tests, but neither path converted tests into an accepted build; both official evaluations failed at compilation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed the full 2,400 second cell budget, timed out with return code 143, and the workflow state was killed after repeated stalled-agent retries.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed in about 953 seconds and returned with 1,445 seconds of budget remaining, despite leaving the implementation incomplete.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel suffered a coordination-specific budget exhaustion event; serial failed from ordinary incomplete implementation rather than process timeout.

outcome_analysis.explanation: There is no discordant official outcome: both current completed cell/status.json evaluations report solution_passed false with compile_failed and 1,387 not-run tests. The material difference is process and coverage, not score: parallel spent the whole budget on a broad workflow plus partial implementation, while serial completed its process with time left but submitted an even smaller partial source tree.
parallel_contributors: Broad workflow fan-out with repeated stalled-agent retries consumed closure budget before integration and build completion.
Parent implementation remained partial even though some child behavioral probes produced notes and tests.
serial_contributors: The serial process completed without delegation and with budget remaining.
The serial implementation was still only a small subset of a Lua interpreter, so it also failed to compile.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel wrote more parser/lexer/object skeleton files; serial wrote memory/table/header files and stopped before conversions and lexer work.
Both lacked the complete buildable interpreter required by the benchmark, which is an ordinary implementation shortfall shared by both attempts.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no official outcome difference; retained pattern is a realized adverse parallel process contributor only

Rejected as less specific than the observed broad fan-out and repeated retry budget exhaustion across many live children.

Retained because the parent created a 16-area workflow, the workflow state records repeated stalled-agent retries and killed status, and the official run timed out before implementation/build closure.
candidates.realized_consequence: The workflow consumed the available run budget and was killed before the parent completed, assembled, or verified a buildable Lua interpreter.
candidates.near_match_reason: The harm came from collective fan-out breadth and retry churn rather than a single demonstrably oversized child scope.

retained_patterns.reason: The parallel run fanned out across 16 Lua behavior areas and then retried stalled children; the workflow was killed and the agent process timed out before a coherent implementation/build was delivered. Serial did not use delegation and completed its process, but also failed because its local implementation was unfinished.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: The workflow consumed the available run budget and was killed before the parent completed, assembled, or verified a buildable Lua interpreter.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: Critical-Path Starvation, Oversized Child Task, Early Child Termination, No Failure Takeover, Missing Verifier Return, Unused Completed Result, and Blind Timeout Wait were treated as near matches or downstream symptoms of the same workflow timeout chain.
cardinality_audit.underlabel_check: All 32 Level-3 candidates were audited; only fan-out budget exhaustion cleared the paired retention gate with distinct adverse consequence.
cardinality_audit.overlabel_check: Only one label was retained for the single broad workflow timeout chain, avoiding duplicate labels for downstream missing results or cancelled progress.
